newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Jews call for Allianz boycott.
newsitem.headline: French Jews call for Allianz boycott.

text.p: A French Jewish group called on Monday for a boycott of German insurance group Allianz AG Holding after a U.S. lawsuit alleged it had benefited from Nazi persecution of Jews.
The FFDJF association of descendants of French Jews deported to death camps called on the public not to take out an insurance policy with Allianz until the group took steps to compensate victims.

Allianz has launched a campaign to help relatives of Holocaust victims track down missing assets after it was named with six other insurers in a class-action lawsuit launched earlier this year in the United States.
The suit alleges that insurers concealed or converted the cash value and proceeds of insurance policies sold before 1946 to mainly Jewish victims of Nazi persecution.
The allegations are similar to those made against some Swiss banks alleged to have profited from the Hitler regime.

Allianz management board member Herbert Hansmeyer has told Germany's Der Spiegel magazine that Allianz was contemplating a fund similar to that established by Swiss banks even though he said the insurer lost most of its capital after World War Two.
Switzerland has set up a $185 million Holocaust memorial fund with donations from banks and businesses and has proposed a $4.7 billion "Solidarity Foundation" to help victims of human rights abuses.
